newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Regent fund ready to close Ukraine investment fund.
newsitem.headline: Regent fund ready to close Ukraine investment fund.

text.p: Fund manager Regent Pacific Group is preparing to close the second portion of its new $50 million Ukraine investment fund, a company official said on Wednesday.
"We're now in the process of closing the second portion of the fund, which will take place over the next few weeks," Andrew Leasor, representative for the fund in Kiev, told Reuters.
"We should close for the agreed $50 million."
The main focus of the fund, launched late last year, would be industrial firms which Leasor called "bluer chip companies".
These included chemicals manufacturers, agro-industrial firms, utilities, and firms in the oil and gas sector, transportation and financial services.
"We hope to end up with holdings in up to 20 companies. That's not many, but it's enough," he said.

Leasor said investment volumes in the Ukrainian equities market were expected to grow in 1997 as investors moved away from the Treasury bill market, where high returns started to diminish in mid-1996.
"There will be exponential growth this year," Leasor said.
The Hong Kong- and London-based company has concentrated its efforts on Russian, other Eastern European, and Asian markets.
